To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the oxygen consumption of the placenta is diminished in toxemia of pregnancy and that this decrease in metabolic activity correlates well with clinical severity.

1) the metabolic activity of the human placenta is directly related to the oxygen tension of the uteroplacental circulation; and 2) in toxemia, placental ischemia is associated with decreased placental oxygen consumption, and the degree of hypoxia is related to the severity of the clinical syndrome.
the placenta from patients with toxemia of pregnancy has diminished oxygen consumption, while the placenta from hypertensive cardiovascular disease patients has normal oxygen consumption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental system to evaluate the effects of maternal and placental factors on fetal oxygenation.
the development of a simple, rapid, reproducible, and sensitive method for measuring the oxygen utilization of the human placenta in vitro.
the metabolic activity of the human placenta.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the placental metabolic activity of pre-eclamptic patients was depressed in relation to the severity of the syndrome, while the placental oxygen consumption in patients with hypertensive disease was elevated in relation to the degree of hypertension, and that patients with documented renal disease showed only moderate elevations in placental metabolic activity.
placental oxygen consumption is a function of the severity of the underlying disorder.

the placenta is a highly sensitive organ, capable of reflecting a wide variety of physiologic and pathologic conditions, and that its metabolic activity is an excellent indicator of the degree of placental insufficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the placenta is a sensitive indicator of the presence of maternal toxemia.
placental hypoxia, as measured by oxygen consumption, was found associated with pre-eclampsia, but not with hypertensive cardiovascular or renal disease.
the placenta, as an organ of exchange, is a sensitive index of the adequacy of maternal blood supply.
The main takeaway from our work is that
placental oxygen consumption is not a reliable index of the severity of toxemia.
placental oxygen consumption is not a good marker for placental function.
the placenta is not a static structure.
